prerequisites: Basic knowledge of the Finite Element Method is recommended, but not mandatory

learning_outcomes.text: Have insight into various techniques of Computer Aided Engineering (CAE).
Can apply CAE methods such as FEM, CFD, and MKS to engineering problems.
Understand CAE as an integral part of virtual product development.
Are able to create numerical models as a digital representation of real mechanical structures and components on the computer.
Understand the fundamental relationships of advanced strength of materials.
Possess in-depth knowledge of the Finite Element Method.
Can competently apply FEM in the areas of structural mechanics and temperature field calculation and independently define appropriate boundary conditions.
Possess knowledge of multi-body simulation and fluid flow simulation.
Know the peculiarities and physical backgrounds of nonlinear calculations and can perform, evaluate, and discuss nonlinear structural mechanical calculations.
Possess knowledge of crash simulation and can assess the peculiarities of this simulation.
Possess knowledge of the numerical solution of systems of differential equations and can apply these methods.
Are able to solve technical calculation problems independently or in a team, also in the nonlinear domain, dynamics, and optimization.
Possess the ability to evaluate, communicate, and discuss CAE results.
Know the possibilities and limitations of numerical methods.
Possess abstraction ability, analytical thinking ability, and a structured approach to solving technical simulation tasks.
Understand CAE as an important method for digitalization in mechanical engineering, know the theoretical backgrounds, and can apply computer-aided methods in the development process.

syllabus_topics: Basic knowledge of the FEM method – review and continuation, thermal and thermo-elastic analyses
Application of FEM in temperature field calculation, for calculating thermal stresses, and for solving static and dynamic structural mechanical problems
Special methods of FEM modeling in structural mechanics
Selected topics such as crash calculation
Integration of CAE into the development process
Independent processing and presentation of CAE tasks
assessment_rules: The assessment is a 90-minute written exam. Students can earn bonus points, up to approximately 6% of the possible exam score, by independently working on and presenting a simulation task alone or in a team. These bonus points are added to the exam performance.
